# Verdict — land-cover recovery-gap diagnostic

**(i) The ordering is in the target before any model.** In the recovery-gap target cropland scores 0.480 and forest 0.248 (difference +0.231; medians 0.517 vs 0.160) — cropland is higher, not lower — and the difference comes from the denominator rather than from recovery: the two classes lost similar absolute NBR between 2017 and 2025 (0.047 vs 0.039), but cropland's 2017 reference level is half of forest's (0.108 vs 0.215) [t04a, t04b].

**(ii) Fire timing does not explain it.** The classes did burn at different times — median first fire Jul 2018 for cropland vs Oct 2023 for forest, 61 vs 39 months before the 2025 window, KS D = 0.41 [t01b, t01c] — but in the wrong direction (forest had less time to recover yet has the lower gap), and with recovery time held at 77-79 months in the 2018-2019 cohort the ordering persists (Spearman ρ = 0.93 over 7 classes; 0.96 for single-fire pixels; 1.00 timing-standardised) while cropland − forest narrows from 0.23 to 0.13-0.19 [t05a, t05b]: timing inflates that pairwise difference but does not create the ordering.

**(iii) Baseline seasonality contributes only through the same denominator.** The absolute 2016-2017 seasonal amplitude does not track the target (r = 0.02 across 9 classes; within-class pixel Spearman ρ = 0.08); amplitude correlates only once divided by the annual baseline mean (r = 0.84, 7 classes, descriptive), which is the low-baseline normalisation effect again rather than an independent contribution [t06b, t06c].

**(iv) The model mirrors the target, and the target does not measure recovery.** Per-class model means reproduce the target almost exactly (recovery gap r = 0.9998, ρ = 1.00, identical ordering over 7 classes, largest class-mean difference 0.015; severity r = 0.998; persistence r = 0.9999; only the threshold-derived recurrence departs, r = 0.72) [t03a, t03b], whereas NBR measured on each pixel's own fire shows no class ordering once calendar period is held fixed — for 2018-2019 single fires every class with n ≥ 500 is back within -0.010 to +0.032 NBR of its pre-fire level by year 2 (forest -0.001, cropland +0.007, grassland +0.012; forest's apparent -0.087 depression belongs to its Oct 2023-centred fires) [t02b] while the same cohort's target spans 0.10-0.67 [t05a] — so the result should be described as the model reproducing spectral, baseline-normalised NBR patterns built into its target, not ecological recovery differences between land covers.

Table ids in brackets refer to `diagnostics/nb13_landcover_timing/tables/nb13_<id>_*.csv`.
